summary: Iteration 4 (CampionAI Plus + payments) tested end-to-end. Backend: new pytest suite (23 tests) for Plus gating (402), 14-day app-managed trial, wellness plan generate/toggle/regenerate, AI food macro logging + totals + delete, schedule CRUD/sorting, Stripe Flow B checkout (plus_monthly/plus_yearly/donate_15) + status polling, cross-user isolation, and chat streaming for a Plus user. Full backend suite = 75/75 passed. Frontend: full UI journey (register @campionqa.com -> 4-step onboarding -> chat -> Upgrade to Plus -> paywall -> start trial -> 3 tabs) all passed; Stripe redirect verified for Subscribe monthly and Donate $15 (checkout.stripe.com URLs); payment cancel + success(pending->'Still processing') pages render; unauth /wellness redirects to /auth; regression (escalation card with 3 hotlines + 'Trusted contact on file' + verified professional, handoff dialog, mic-button present, voice-toggle hidden, admin login with all 4 tabs) passed. Mobile 390px: no horizontal overflow. No blocking bugs found.

minor.issue: No authentication/ownership check. Any caller holding a session_id can poll status and trigger _grant_access for another user's transaction. Session ids are secret-ish, but add Depends(get_current_user) + user_id match.
_grant_access sets plus.trial_used=True when a subscription is paid, so a user who pays first can never later use the free 14-day trial (start-trial then returns 400). Confirm this is intended.
Without ?date it returns ALL events for the user (limit 500) with no pagination; will grow unbounded over time.

integration_issues.issue: loadPlusData() has no try/catch — if /wellness/plan (LLM) fails, the promise rejects silently and the page stays empty with no error state/retry UI. All other calls (toggle, delFood, addEvent, delEvent) also lack error handling/toasts.

Cosmetic/UX: regenerate returns a new plan doc (verified new id in backend) but the LLM often produces near-identical titles, so the UI looks unchanged after 'New plan' — consider a visible confirmation/diff or higher temperature.

issues: Trusted-contact/professional sub-line is rendered with title-case capitalization ('Friend · Reach Out To Them Directly If You Can'), which reads oddly for a sentence — use normal sentence case.
Time input + title input + add button on one row makes the title placeholder truncate ('Add something to y…'); consider stacking on small screens.
Uses native browser time picker (input type=time) rather than a styled component — acceptable, but visually inconsistent with the dark Obsidian theme.

action_items: Add auth + ownership check to GET /api/payments/status/{session_id}
Add error handling (try/catch + toast/retry) around loadPlusData and the wellness mutations in Wellness.js
Decide/document whether paying should consume the free trial (plus.trial_used=True in _grant_access)
Fix sentence-case for escalation card trusted-contact/professional sub-line
Consider splitting server.py (1046 lines) into routers: payments/plus/wellness vs chat/safety/admin
critical_code_review_comments: payments_status has no auth dependency yet mutates user entitlement via _grant_access — gate it to the owning user.
server.py is 1046 lines (>700 guideline); wellness + payments are self-contained and should move to their own routers.
Wellness.js shares a single `busy` flag across trial/checkout/regenerate/food, so unrelated buttons disable together during a slow LLM call.

Amounts are correctly taken server-side from PACKAGES (no client-supplied price) and metadata carries user_id/package_id — good Stripe hygiene; webhook + status both funnel through idempotent _grant_access (granted flag).

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows passed (no blocking UI bugs)

SSE event type for chat deltas is 'delta' (not 'chunk'). Wellness paywall testids: plan-plus_monthly/plan-plus_yearly, subscribe-plus_{monthly,yearly}, start-trial-button, donate-donate_{5,15,30}. rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects reproduced. Only real finding: /api/payments/status/{session_id} is unauthenticated while it can flip a payment_transactions row to paid and grant Plus via _grant_access; an attacker who learns/guesses a session id could poll (and, if that session was actually paid by someone else, cause the grant to be applied to the transaction owner — not privilege escalation for the attacker, but it removes access control from a billing endpoint).
